title: Quadratic class and unit groups
objective: Audit and close integrated quadratic public-routing gaps, including alternate presentations, ideal maps, algorithm validation, imaginary-route regression coverage, and honest large-discriminant capability bounds

handoff.summary: Audited the integrated degree-two routes and extended the strict quadratic backend with Sage-compatible algorithm validation, a presentation-independent canonical ideal-lattice map, a public-field continued-fraction unit adapter, an exact preflight cost plan, a default 5,000,000-candidate enumeration cap, and deterministic unsigned-64-bit primality acceleration. Focused public coverage now preserves the imaginary D=-23 route under two presentations, checks real D=60 standard/translated presentations and ideal maps, transports D=12 units exactly, and verifies a fundamental discriminant above signed 64-bit range is represented exactly but rejected before infeasible exhaustive enumeration. The focused suite and strict 208-module gate pass on linux-x64.
risks: The quadratic-forms class-group algorithm remains exhaustive O(D), materializes every reduced form, and defaults to max_enumeration_checks=5,000,000. It now fails before enumeration when the exact candidate estimate exceeds the cap; buchmann-hecke and minkowski are recognized but explicitly unavailable.

Deterministic primality acceleration removes the signed-word restriction through unsigned 64-bit inputs. Fundamental-discriminant validation beyond that range remains exact trial division and can be slow; a mature arbitrary-precision factoring backend is still needed for uniformly fast huge unit computations.

The shared public baselib has not been edited in this lane. Its real class-group inverse ideal map still computes coordinates in the defining maximal-order basis, so translated presentations need the supplied canonical-basis routing patch; imaginary-backend inverse ideal coercion remains explicitly unsupported.
The offline Magma command is recorded but no Magma executable was available in this workspace; the committed numerical corpus was executed against SageMath 10.9.post30/PARI 2.18.1.
Only linux-x64 was executed in this lane; native Windows x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64 validation remains a central integration responsibility.
next_steps: Integration lane should route real quadratic unit_group to real_quadratic_field_unit_group and forward algorithm/max_steps; route real class_group/class_number algorithm and resource limits to real_quadratic_class_group while retaining the existing imaginary backend.

Integration lane should express ideals in the canonical [1, (D%2+sqrt(D))/2] basis and call quadratic_form_from_ideal_lattice. This changes translated D=60 ideal (2, a) from the invalid form (2,0,-8) to (2,2,-7).

Run pnpm test:changed, pnpm test:native, and exact-revision four-platform CI after merging all number-field lanes. The local test:changed attempt was stopped during generated-runtime stage 4 after focused and strict gates passed; an earlier build passed stages 1-6 but native-kernel publication did not finish promptly.
Oracle lane may replace the recorded Magma command metadata with an executed Magma receipt when a licensed executable is available.
